method: Static reverse engineering only; Ghidra decompilation, Rizin disassembly, dnfile/dncil IL, PE parsing, atomscan and cleave facts. No sample code executed.

samples.identity: Rifaien self-submission wrapper containing an intact native modular service backdoor
samples.scope: Verdict reflects the contained executable implant. The wrapper is a self-submission utility; its upload is not theft of user files. No execution of the appended implant by the wrapper was established.
evidence: Outer entry 0x401130 reaches main 0x4013a0. Main reads its own image, randomizes 16 bytes after [[UNIQUE]], writes a clone and submits it using libcurl multipart file[]/node/submit, then deletes the clone and repeats after a sleep.
Appended PE at file offset 0x3b000 has a complete executable entry and native implant logic. Extracted and decompiled independently.
Implant 0x4027e0 sends host/OS/user information, reads socket records, dispatches byte six 0x88 to writing DLL bytes and 0x89 to writing and ShellExecute-ing a replacement executable.
0x402550 loads the uploaded module and invokes Load, Run, Stop and Unload exports.
0x4043f0 creates the implant service with SERVICE_AUTO_START (2) and SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS|SERVICE_INTERACTIVE_PROCESS (0x110), and configures restart actions.

0x403350 complements every other byte in strided buffers, recovering dynamic-DNS hosts and DLL-upload/load status messages. Existing concealed-dispatch and service traits accurately describe the embedded executable.

samples.identity: E-language Wulin Waizhuan game automation helper with MicroSu answer plugin
evidence: Chinese UI and game code target elementclient.exe: character/skill selection, combat, potion thresholds, automatic login and configuration files. Process/memory manipulation is consistent with the game helper.
0x420079 startup checks connectivity and reaches SMTP helper 0x4209ab. That helper initializes SMTP with embedded account settings; its subject/body values come from two calls to 0x420bad.

0x420bad fetches the IP138 public-IP page and extracts text between the Chinese IP-address delimiters. The mail path reports this public IP, not the game username/password controls or arbitrary files.
The two information INI paths are passed through deletion calls before SMTP setup; they are not read and attached as loot in this path.
Embedded MicroSu.dll is a VB6 COM plugin with an HTTP answer/image-upload interface, registered by the game helper. This is consistent with the visible answer-plugin UI.
SMTP MIME Base64 text belongs to a linked general-purpose mail implementation. Global atom APIs and WriteProcessMemory coexist, but no atom-name-to-APC injection path was found.
The third-party Chinese/Hacktool matcher requires generic MFC/UI, Reply-To, User-Agent and HTML-extension strings. It establishes no hostile identity.

samples.identity: Compiled ASP.NET cs86nt.aspx native-thread HTTPS shellcode stager
evidence: Managed ASP.mobile_cs86nt_aspx.Page_Load at RVA 0x78cc initializes an 836-byte embedded buffer, loads ntdll, resolves NtAllocateVirtualMemory and converts its pointer to a delegate.

Page_Load allocates MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE (0x3000), PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE (0x40), copies the byte buffer into the allocation using Marshal.Copy, and invokes NtCreateThreadEx in the current process at that address.
The buffer starts at FieldRVA 0x7588 (file 0x6588). Its x86 PEB/export walker hashes module/API names with ROR13.
Shellcode loads wininet, creates an HTTPS request to configured host 154.204.58.234:443, and uses hashed WinINet API calls. Endpoint/path values are not detection gates.

At shellcode offset 0x2ef it allocates RWX stage memory. Offset 0x30f repeatedly calls InternetReadFile (hash 0xe2899612), advances the destination by bytes read, and at EOF RET transfers execution into the stage.

The page is a web-triggered native stager, not an assembly module loader. The payload is x86 despite a diagnostic message claiming 64-bit. NtCreateThreadEx here creates a local thread and does not prove remote-process injection.

changes: Retire SMTP HELO/MIME/WinINet and multipart mutation-marker exfiltration claims without a stolen source-to-send chain.
Retire generic mutex/crypto/HTTP coordination claim and remove it as a persistence alternative.
Remove atom-bombing-capable: memory writing or thread-context APIs do not establish atom bombing. Existing consumers now require the APC-specific observation.
Disable the unsupported generic Chinese/Hacktool identity; classify generic shellcode references suspicious independently of malicious activation.
Move the compiled ASP.NET stager to webshell/stager and require the API-hashed receive-to-execution signature.
Remove bare NtCreateThreadEx text from the remote-thread API group; retain its neutral thread-name trait.
Keep regsvr32 command references notable even in PEs carrying resources.
